# `system_log`

`system_log` writes one line for each alert to the delivering machine's
systemd journal: the alert's title with its severity in front.
An example title is `SOS: web-3: myapp/http failed`. MMWatchdog writes the
line itself, through the journal's own socket, and needs no other program.

Choose `system_log` when the machine's log already goes somewhere.
A product that collects the system log of the product's machines carries
the alerts further through the product's log collection and needs no other destination. To reach people directly, use [`email`](email.md),
an official extra module such
as [`slack`](../../../official_extra_modules/slack/README.md), or
[`mmhotline`](mmhotline.md). A destination names its module and
states the settings that every destination takes, as [the alert destinations file](../configuration-files.md#the-alert-destinations-file) describes.

The `system_log` module has no inputs, so the module's value is `{}`.

## Inputs

The module takes no inputs.

## What it sends

The `system_log` destination writes one journal entry for each alert, with
these fields:

- **The message** is the alert's
  [title with the alert's severity in front](../alert-format.md),
  such as `SOS: web-3: myapp/http failed` or
  `Resolved SOS: web-3: myapp/http is ok again`.
- **The identifier is `mmwatchdog-alert`,** so `journalctl --identifier mmwatchdog-alert`
  shows the alerts and nothing else. The daemon's own messages are in the
  journal of its unit, `mmwatchdog.service`.
- **The priority follows the alert's severity:** critical for `sos`,
  warning for `warn`, and informational for `info`. An alert that closes an
  incident, a recovery, a check that MMWatchdog can check again, or a retirement, is
  informational whatever the severity of the incident was. So a log
  collector that acts on the priority does not take the end of an outage for
  a new outage.

The alert's body is not written. `mmwatchdog events` on the node has the whole
event. Because `system_log` writes only the title,
`send_only_the_alert_title` is refused on a `system_log` destination, as a
validation error.

## When a delivery fails

A line that the journal does not accept is a failed attempt, such as when
the journal's socket `/run/systemd/journal/socket` does not exist or does
not take the line within `time_limit_per_delivery_attempt`, `5s` unless the
destination states another time. The error reads
`MMWatchdog could not write the alert to the system log: ...`, with the reason. MMWatchdog
tries again as for every destination: after one second, then with the delay
doubling up to 256 seconds
([delivery](../../how-it-works.md#the-outbox-and-delivery)), and
`mmwatchdog status` shows the destination as
[a destination that is failing](../../when-something-fails.md#a-destination-is-failing).

## Examples

### Every alert in the system log

```yaml
# /etc/mmwatchdog/alert_destinations.yml
destinations:
  machine_log:
    remind_every: never
    system_log: {}                    # one line in the system log for each alert
    alert_severities: [info, warn, sos]
```

The check `http` in the check group `myapp`, with `alert_severity: sos`,
fails on the standalone node `web-3`. MMWatchdog on `web-3` writes the line to the
node's journal, at the priority critical. The `journalctl` output below shows
the alert entry:

```text
$ journalctl --identifier mmwatchdog-alert
Sep 29 14:07:05 web-3 mmwatchdog-alert[812]: SOS: web-3: myapp/http failed
```

When the check recovers, MMWatchdog writes
`Resolved SOS: web-3: myapp/http is ok again` at the priority informational.
`journalctl --identifier mmwatchdog-alert --priority warning` shows only the lines
of `warn` and `sos` alerts.

### The system log beside a mailbox

```yaml
# /etc/mmwatchdog/alert_destinations.yml
destinations:
  machine_log:
    remind_every: never
    system_log: {}
    alert_severities: [info, warn, sos]
  operations_mailbox:
    remind_every: never
    email:
      smtp_server: localhost:25        # the mail server on this same machine
      smtp_connection_security: unencrypted
      from: mmwatchdog@app-1.example.com
      to: [operations@example.com]
    alert_severities: [warn, sos]
```

Every alert goes to the journal, and the `warn` and `sos` alerts also go by
email. Each destination has its own queue, so a mail server that does not
answer never holds up the lines in the journal.

## Test the destination

Reload and daily [quiet verification](../../how-it-works.md#the-outbox-and-delivery)
open the journal socket through MMWatchdog's shared connection primitive without
writing an entry. To test the complete path,
send a notice explicitly as shown below.

Send a [notice](../commands.md#mmwatchdog-send-notice) to the destination alone,
then look for the notice's line:

```text
$ sudo mmwatchdog send-notice --alert-severity info --title "Test of the system log. Nothing is wrong." --destination machine_log
Notice sent to the destination machine_log:
  machine_log   delivered
$ journalctl --identifier mmwatchdog-alert --lines 1
Sep 29 14:10:12 web-3 mmwatchdog-alert[812]: Info: web-3: Test of the system log. Nothing is wrong.
```

## How it works

- **The line is written on the machine that delivers the alert.** A
  standalone node writes the line to the standalone node's journal. In a
  fleet, the destination is in the hub's `alert_destinations.yml`, and the hub
  writes the alerts of all its joined nodes to the hub's own journal.
  A joined node writes a line to its
  own journal only for an alert that it delivers without the hub
  ([alerts in a fleet](../../how-to/set-up-a-fleet.md#where-alerts-go-in-a-fleet)).

## Errors and what they mean

| Error | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `destinations.machine_log.send_only_the_alert_title: a system_log destination takes no send_only_the_alert_title: it writes only the title with the alert's severity in front` | Remove the setting: the line holds only the title already |
| `destinations.machine_log.system_log: the module system_log takes no inputs and is written system_log: {}` | Write `system_log: {}`, not `system_log:` with nothing after it |
| `destinations.machine_log.system_log.facility: unknown field "facility": the module system_log takes no inputs` | The module has no inputs. Write `system_log: {}` |
| `failed: MMWatchdog could not write the alert to the system log: ...` | The journal did not take the line. Check that `systemd-journald` runs on the machine that delivers the alert |

MMWatchdog prefixes a validation error with the setting's configuration file
and line, such as
`/etc/mmwatchdog/alert_destinations.yml:4:5:`.

## Tested on

- **Go tests,** on macOS and natively on
  [every target distribution](../../changing-mmwatchdog/testing.md#every-target-distribution):
  `TestSystemLogDestination` in `internal/checksandalerts/node_checks_test.go`, against
  a stand-in for the journal's socket: entries for `sos` and `warn` failures,
  a reminder, a maintenance alert, and two alerts that close an
  incident; a journal that takes no entry
  as a failed attempt; a message of several lines; the settings of the
  destination and the refusal of
  `send_only_the_alert_title`; and the destination read back from JSON.
- **VM suites,** on [every target distribution](../../changing-mmwatchdog/testing.md#every-target-distribution): the node scenarios
  (`tests/integration/node_scenarios.py`) find a failure and its recovery in
  the guest's real journal, under the identifier `mmwatchdog-alert`, with the
  priorities critical and informational.

## Why it works this way

- **Quiet verification opens the socket without writing.** Reload checks
  whether the journal can be reached without producing a test alert.
- **Destination health waits ten minutes before notifying other destinations.**
  Temporary failures and delivery retries have time to clear. The
  [shared delivery rules](../../when-something-fails.md#a-destination-is-failing)
  own the fixed delay and notices.

- **The system log is a core destination.** Every Linux server has one, and
  a product that ships MMWatchdog inside the product carries the alerts through its own log
  collection.
- **One line, the title with the severity in front.** A log line is read in
  a list of many, and the title is complete in one line. The whole event
  stays in `mmwatchdog events`.
- **The identifier `mmwatchdog-alert` is not the daemon's.** A person or a log
  collector selects the alerts without the daemon's own messages.
- **An alert that closes an incident is informational.** A log collector
  that alerts on the priority must not take the end of an outage for a new
  one.
- **MMWatchdog writes to the journal's socket itself.** A node needs no program
  such as `logger` to deliver an alert.
